name: Windows 1.0
tagline: The first Windows — a desktop dithered from two colors to fake a third.
description: Windows 1.0 (1985) was Microsoft's first graphical shell, running tiled windows over MS-DOS. Limited to a fixed hardware palette, it couldn't display its signature desktop green directly — so it dithered it, tiling 8×8 blocks of bright green with 4×4 patches of cyan to blend a softer shade the hardware couldn't name. Depending on how you average that pattern, the result lands near #57ff81 (a simple pixel average) or #57ff9a (averaged in linear light, gamma-corrected).

colors.name: Dithered Green (Averaged)
colors.note: The Windows 1.0 desktop. There was no single green for it in the hardware palette, so the desktop was dithered — 8×8 blocks of green (#57ff57) with a 4×4 patch of cyan (#57ffff) inside each, 25% cyan by area. This is the conventional pixel average of that pattern; averaging in linear light instead gives the gamma-corrected #57ff9a.

colors.name: Dithered Green (Gamma-Corrected)
colors.note: The same dithered desktop, but averaged in linear light and gamma-corrected — a slightly mintier green. The simpler pixel average is #57ff81.

colors.name: Phosphor Green
colors.note: One of the two colors the Windows 1.0 desktop was dithered from — the green that fills each 8×8 block.

colors.name: Aqua
colors.note: One of the two colors the Windows 1.0 desktop was dithered from — the cyan filling a 4×4 patch inside each 8×8 green block (25% by area).
